question.leadin: Answer the following about the Conway Cabal.
question.text: One member of the Conway Cabal, James Wilkinson, was later involved in the possibly-treasonous activities of this man, who narrowly lost to Jefferson in the 1800 presidential election and shot Alexander Hamilton in a duel.
question.clue: This politician was involved in a plot with "Number Thirteen," a Spanish agent and US Army officer named James Wilkinson, leading to this politician being tried for treason.

swap.text: This second president of the US was the only president ever officially elected as a Federalist.
swap.answerHtml: John Adams [do not accept or prompt on “John Quincy Adams”]
swap.clue: This man said "facts are stubborn things" during his defense of John Preston for his role in the Boston Massacre.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about a certain political party in American history.
question.text: Name this party, led by Alexander Hamilton, that opposed the Democratic-Republicans.
question.clue: The Coodies were a faction of this party from Maryland.

swap.leadin: In the early 1800s, Napoleon gave up on building a French empire in the New World.
swap.text: Napoleon sold this territory of nearly one million square miles of land to the United States in 1803.
swap.clue: This was the territory exchanged in the Treaty of Fontainebleau, which was returned to France before being bought by the US in 1803.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the 1832 Reform Act.
question.text: The Reform Act was passed while Earl Grey, a member of this party, was prime minister. This party opposed the Tories.
question.clue: Benjamin Curtis, the only man to be appointed to the Supreme Court as a member of this group, resigned after dissenting from the Dred Scott decision.

swap.leadin: This battle's namesake mission in San Antonio was defended by such men as Davy Crockett.
swap.text: Name this battle in which Mexican soldiers slaughtered the defending Texans, led by Colonel Travis.
swap.clue: During this battle, a letter was addressed to "all Americans in the World" and signed "Victory or Death" by losing commander William Barret Travis.

question.text: The Specie Circular was issued by this U.S. president, who liquidated the Second Bank of the U.S. This man created the "Trail of Tears" by ordering the forced march of the Cherokee and other tribes from their homeland.
question.clue: This man dismantled the Second Bank of the United States, and he fought in the First Seminole War.

swap.leadin: The clash alternately called the Battle of Jupiter Inlet or the First Battle of Loxahatchee occurred during this war.
swap.text: Name this war in which one group was led by a man born as Billy Powell who was later given the name Osceola. This war began a few years after the signing of the Treaty of Payne's Landing.
swap.answerHtml: Second Seminole War [prompt on Seminole War; prompt on but otherwise do not reveal Florida War]
swap.clue: During this war, Quartermaster General Thomas Jesup captured an enemy leader who arrived for a meeting under a white flag of truce.

question.leadin: One death that occurred on this vessel was perpetrated by Joseph Cinque [sin-kay], who led many captives onboard in an uprising that killed Ramon Ferrez.
question.text: Name this ship that was the site of a revolt, and eventually landed on Long Island, where the passengers were taken back into captivity.
question.clue: African-American slaves on this Spanish ship led a mutiny against its crew. After the slaves were tried for their crimes on this ship, they were sent back to their native countries.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about an episode in U.S.-France relations per part.
swap.text: In this 1797 incident, the French foreign minister demanded a bribe from American treaty negotiators, leading to a naval skirmishes and the Convention of 1800.
swap.clue: Following this incident, the president gave a speech advocating the creation of a navy for defense.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the early 19th century's hippest economic platform, the American System.
question.text: The American System called for investment in American infrastructure, leading to the completion of projects like the Erie Canal and this railroad. It was the first chartered railroad in American history.
question.clue: The Great Railroad Strike of 1877 began in response to this railroad cutting wages three times in one year.

swap.text: This 1810 case of the Marshall Court is cited as the first time the Supreme Court struck down a state law as unconstitutional. This case involved land speculators on Yazoo tribal lands in Georgia.
swap.answerHtml: Fletcher v. Peck [or Fletcher v. Peck; accept in alternate order]
swap.clue: Georgia's legal malfeasanse did not end there, as the state's invalidation of contracts for Yazoo River lands led to this 1810 case, which held that the contracts clause bound the states.

question.leadin: This time period got its name from reporter Benjamin Russell during the president's tour of the northeast.
question.text: Name this period of American history. The first two-party system collapsed before this period in which the Democratic-Republicans were the only party.
question.clue: This period of American history succeeded the War of 1812. It was characterized by a common sense of nationalism, optimism, and positivity, and coincided with the presidency of James Monroe.

swap.leadin: Name these Americans killed in famous duels.
swap.text: This admiral, hero of the Barbary Wars and War of 1812, remains the youngest ever to have been a captain in the U.S. Navy. He was fatally wounded by Commodore James Barron; his shot smashed Barron's hip.
swap.clue: Benjamin Latrobe built this man a house in Lafayette Square, where this victor over the Macedonian became a Washington celebrity.

question.leadin: The eastern end of this landmark was also the northwestern terminus of the still-extant Chesapeake and Ohio Canal, allowing goods to be loaded onto boats and taken to Washington, D.C.
question.text: Name this early federal public works project, which extended west from Maryland to Vandalia, Illinois.
question.clue: This road, whose alternate name refers to the namesake Maryland city from which it extended to Vandalia, Illinois, was never completed, as it ran out of funding in 1839. Its construction was part of Henry Clay's American System.

swap.leadin: This man was called an "incurable lunatic" by Jeffersonians for the staunchly pro-Federalist content he published in his newspaper American Minerva.
swap.text: Name this newspaper editor, who created a book nicknamed for its blue cover that sold over 50 million copies by 1890.
swap.clue: One book by this man is nicknamed for its blue backing.

question.text: Vetoing legislation that would improve the nation's infrastructure, just like expanding the voting rolls, was a hallmark of Jacksonian Democracy. James K. Polk pocket vetoed an 1846 bill that would have spent $1.4 million to improve these two types of waterways.

swap.text: In the 1790s, this African-American polymath created an early American almanac and included his dialogues with Thomas Jefferson on slavery. This man is also attributed with creating the first American-made clock.
swap.clue: This African American architect and astronomer reconstructed Pierre L'Enfant's layout for Washington D.C. from memory.

question.text: After he was appointed to the Supreme Court, Taney decided this landmark 1837 contracts case from Massachusetts that confirmed the right of all Americans to build the a certain type of structure
question.answer: Charles River Bridge v. Warren Bridge
question.clue: The plaintiff in this 1837 Supreme Court case tried to cite the Dartmouth case in complaining that the state of Massachusetts violated a 1785 charter that concerned traffic near the city of Boston.

swap.leadin: Name these Supreme Court decisions arising out of Virginia.
swap.text: Arising out of a refusal by Virginia to abide by the decision in the Fairfax's Devisee case, this 1816 ruling said that the Judiciary Act of 1789 remained constitutional and Virginia had best abide by the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction or else.
swap.clue: This 1816 case in which the Supreme Court ruled that it did have jurisdiction to rule on cases that originated in state courts.
